project_specification.overview: Extends AutoForge with three post-build agent types that close the gap between "code that works locally" and "code that runs reliably in production with ongoing maintenance." The CI/CD Pipeline Generator creates GitHub Actions workflows, Dockerfiles, and platform-specific deployment configs. The Monitoring Setup Agent adds Sentry error tracking, health endpoints, structured logging, and optional analytics. The Auto-Update Agent runs on a recurring schedule to update dependencies, fix vulnerabilities, verify nothing broke, and create PRs or roll back with issue reports. These are additions to the existing AutoForge codebase (FastAPI + React 19 + TypeScript).

frontend.framework: React 19 with Vite 7 (existing AutoForge UI in ui/)
frontend.state_management: TanStack Query, React hooks and context

backend.runtime: Python 3.11+ with FastAPI and uvicorn (existing AutoForge server)
backend.database: SQLite with SQLAlchemy (existing features.db and registry.db)

communication.api: REST endpoints via FastAPI routers, WebSocket for real-time updates

additional_libraries.node: None new -- templates reference project dependencies, not AutoForge dependencies

prerequisites.environment_setup: - Python 3.11+ with pip - Node.js 20+ with npm (for UI development) - Existing AutoForge installation (source checkout or npm global install) - Claude Code CLI configured and authenticated - ruff and mypy for Python linting/type-checking

core_features.cli_agent_types: - System accepts --agent-type cicd, monitoring, and auto-update as valid choices in autonomous_agent_demo.py alongside existing initializer, coding, and testing types - System accepts --deployment-target flag with choices vercel, railway, flyio, aws, docker for the CI/CD agent - System accepts --monitoring-features flag with comma-separated values (sentry, health, logging, analytics, uptime) defaulting to sentry,health,logging - System accepts --analytics-provider flag with choices plausible, posthog, none defaulting to none - System accepts --update-strategy flag with choices conservative and aggressive defaulting to conservative - System accepts --maintenance-frequency flag with choices weekly, biweekly, monthly defaulting to weekly - System accepts --dry-run boolean flag for the auto-update agent to check without applying updates
core_features.cicd_prompt_template: - System provides CI/CD prompt template at .claude/templates/cicd_prompt.template.md with instructions for generating GitHub Actions CI/staging/production/security workflows, Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, .env.example, Makefile, and platform-specific deployment configs
core_features.monitoring_prompt_template: - System provides monitoring prompt template at .claude/templates/monitoring_prompt.template.md with instructions for adding Sentry error tracking, /api/health endpoint, structured logging middleware, optional analytics (Plausible/PostHog), and uptime monitoring scripts
core_features.auto_update_prompt_template: - System provides auto-update prompt template at .claude/templates/auto_update_prompt.template.md with the five-phase workflow: audit, update, verify, report, and commit-or-rollback with PR creation or issue filing on failure
core_features.cicd_prompt_loading: - System loads the CI/CD template via get_cicd_prompt() in prompts.py and injects the deployment target into the prompt - System auto-detects the deployment target via _detect_deployment_target() by checking for next.config (vercel), fly.toml (flyio), railway.toml (railway), or falling back to docker
core_features.monitoring_and_autoupdate_prompt_loading: - System loads the monitoring template via get_monitoring_prompt() in prompts.py and injects the enabled monitoring features list and analytics provider selection - System loads the auto-update template via get_auto_update_prompt() in prompts.py and injects the update strategy (conservative/aggressive), dry-run flag, and current date for branch naming
core_features.client_configuration: - System configures post-build agents (cicd, monitoring, auto-update) in client.py with no Playwright MCP server, read-only feature MCP tools (feature_get_stats, feature_get_summary only), and standard built-in tools (Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob) - System restricts the CI/CD agent to file generation with full write access to the project directory - System grants the monitoring agent full write access to modify existing project files for instrumentation - System grants the auto-update agent full write access plus git and gh CLI access for branch creation, PR submission, and issue filing
core_features.database_models: - System creates MaintenanceRun model in api/database.py with columns: id (PK), project_name (indexed), run_date, status (success/failure/dry_run), strategy (conservative/aggressive), packages_updated (int), vulnerabilities_fixed (int), tests_passed (bool nullable), pr_url (text nullable), issue_url (text nullable), report_path (text nullable), duration_seconds (int nullable), error_message (text nullable), created_at, updated_at - System extends the Schedule model in api/database.py with schedule_type column (String, default "agent") to distinguish agent schedules from maintenance schedules, and update_strategy column (String, nullable) for maintenance schedule configuration
core_features.maintenance_api: - API returns paginated list of MaintenanceRun records via GET /api/projects/{project_name}/maintenance/history with limit parameter (default 20) - API returns the next scheduled maintenance run date/time via GET /api/projects/{project_name}/maintenance/next-run based on the project's maintenance schedule - API triggers an auto-update agent subprocess via POST /api/projects/{project_name}/maintenance/trigger with optional dry_run boolean parameter - API returns the full maintenance report markdown content via GET /api/projects/{project_name}/maintenance/report/{run_id} for a specific run - API deletes a maintenance run record via DELETE /api/projects/{project_name}/maintenance/history/{run_id} for cleanup of old records - System registers the maintenance router in server/main.py with prefix /api/projects/{project_name}/maintenance
core_features.settings_api: - System exposes DevOps settings in server/routers/settings.py: deployment_target (string), monitoring_features (list of strings), analytics_provider (string), update_strategy (string), maintenance_frequency (string) - System persists DevOps settings via the existing GlobalSettings model in registry.py - API returns DevOps configuration alongside existing settings via GET /api/settings - API accepts DevOps configuration fields alongside existing settings via PUT /api/settings
core_features.scheduler_service: - System extends scheduler_service.py with _handle_scheduled_maintenance() that spawns an auto-update agent subprocess with the schedule's update_strategy - System maps maintenance frequency presets (weekly, biweekly, monthly) to CronTrigger configurations: weekly = Monday 09:00 UTC, biweekly = every other Monday 09:00 UTC, monthly = first Monday of month 09:00 UTC - System handles maintenance schedules (schedule_type="maintenance") separately from agent run schedules (schedule_type="agent") with no interference between the two
core_features.orchestrator_integration: - System detects build completion in parallel_orchestrator.py via _check_post_build_ready() when all features are passing and no post-build agents have run yet - System launches the CI/CD agent via _spawn_cicd_agent() as a single-turn subprocess (no continuation loop) after build completion - System launches the monitoring agent via _spawn_monitoring_agent() as a single-turn subprocess after build completion - System spawns CI/CD and monitoring agents in parallel since they do not conflict (CI/CD writes new files, monitoring modifies existing files in different locations) - System tracks post-build agent status with _cicd_running, _cicd_completed, _monitoring_running, _monitoring_completed flags
core_features.agent_router_support: - System extends server/routers/agent.py to accept cicd, monitoring, and auto-update as valid agent_type values in start and stop endpoints - System passes --deployment-target from settings to the subprocess when starting a cicd agent - System passes --monitoring-features and --analytics-provider from settings to the subprocess when starting a monitoring agent - System passes --update-strategy and optional --dry-run to the subprocess when starting an auto-update agent
core_features.ui_types_and_api_client: - System defines MaintenanceRun TypeScript interface in ui/src/lib/types.ts matching the database model fields - System extends the Schedule type in types.ts with schedule_type and update_strategy fields - System provides maintenance API client functions in ui/src/lib/api.ts: getMaintenanceHistory(), getNextMaintenanceRun(), triggerMaintenance(), getMaintenanceReport(), deleteMaintenanceRun() - System provides TanStack Query hooks in ui/src/hooks/useProjects.ts: useMaintenanceHistory(), useNextMaintenanceRun(), useTriggerMaintenance(), useMaintenanceReport()
core_features.settings_modal_devops: - System extends SettingsModal.tsx with a "DevOps" section containing: deployment target dropdown (Vercel, Railway, Fly.io, AWS, Docker, Auto-detect), monitoring feature checkboxes (Sentry, Health Check, Structured Logging, Analytics, Uptime Monitoring), analytics provider radio buttons (Plausible, PostHog, None), and update strategy toggle (Conservative, Aggressive) - System displays maintenance frequency dropdown (Weekly, Biweekly, Monthly) in the DevOps section - System persists settings changes via PUT /api/settings on save
core_features.maintenance_tab: - System displays MaintenanceTab.tsx component with summary card showing: last maintenance run date and status (green check or red X), next scheduled run date with countdown, current update strategy with toggle, and "Run Now" button that calls POST /trigger - System displays history table with columns: date, status badge, packages updated, vulnerabilities fixed, duration, with each row expandable to show the full maintenance report - System displays schedule configuration section with frequency dropdown, day-of-week selector, time picker (user's local timezone, stored as UTC), and enable/disable toggle - System adds MaintenanceTab to the project view in App.tsx as a new tab alongside existing Kanban/Graph views
core_features.maintenance_report_viewer: - System renders MaintenanceReport.tsx component displaying maintenance report markdown as formatted HTML with sections for summary, dependencies updated table, security audit table, and test results table - System displays a clickable PR link when maintenance succeeded or a clickable issue link when maintenance failed - System makes reports accessible both inline (expanded row in history table) and via direct URL using the run_id - System shows EmptyState when no maintenance runs exist yet, with CTA to configure maintenance schedule or trigger a manual run

tables.maintenance_runs: - id (INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT) - project_name (TEXT NOT NULL, INDEX) - run_date (DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) - status (TEXT NOT NULL, CHECK IN ('success', 'failure', 'dry_run')) - strategy (TEXT NOT NULL, CHECK IN ('conservative', 'aggressive')) - packages_updated (INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0) - vulnerabilities_fixed (INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0) - tests_passed (BOOLEAN, nullable) - pr_url (TEXT, nullable) - issue_url (TEXT, nullable) - report_path (TEXT, nullable) - duration_seconds (INTEGER, nullable) - error_message (TEXT, nullable) - created_at (TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) - updated_at (TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)
tables.schedules_extension: - schedule_type (TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'agent') -- added column: 'agent' or 'maintenance' - update_strategy (TEXT, nullable) -- added column: 'conservative' or 'aggressive', used when schedule_type='maintenance'

api_endpoints_summary.maintenance: - GET /api/projects/{project_name}/maintenance/history?limit=20 (paginated maintenance run list) - GET /api/projects/{project_name}/maintenance/next-run (next scheduled maintenance date/time) - POST /api/projects/{project_name}/maintenance/trigger?dry_run=false (manually trigger maintenance) - GET /api/projects/{project_name}/maintenance/report/{run_id} (full report markdown for a run) - DELETE /api/projects/{project_name}/maintenance/history/{run_id} (delete a maintenance run record)
api_endpoints_summary.settings_extension: - GET /api/settings (extended with deployment_target, monitoring_features, analytics_provider, update_strategy, maintenance_frequency) - PUT /api/settings (extended to accept DevOps configuration fields)
api_endpoints_summary.agent_extension: - POST /api/projects/{project_name}/agent/start (extended to accept agent_type: cicd, monitoring, auto-update) - POST /api/projects/{project_name}/agent/stop (extended to stop post-build agent types)

ui_layout.main_structure: - Existing AutoForge project view with Kanban/Graph tabs - New "Maintenance" tab added to the project view tab bar - Existing Settings modal extended with "DevOps" section - Maintenance tab contains summary card, history table, and schedule configuration

design_system.color_palette: - Uses existing AutoForge neobrutalism design system - Maintenance status colors: success green (--color-neo-done), failure red (error), dry-run blue (info) - Schedule active: cyan (--color-neo-progress), schedule disabled: gray (muted)
design_system.typography: - Follows existing AutoForge typography (Inter, system-ui, sans-serif) - Maintenance report rendered in monospace for tables, proportional for prose
design_system.spacing: - Follows existing AutoForge spacing conventions: 4px grid, standard Tailwind spacing scale - Summary card uses p-6 padding, history table rows use py-3 px-4 - Section gaps use space-y-6 between major sections in the Maintenance tab

ui_ux_standards.banned_patterns: - alert(), confirm(), prompt() -- use existing Modal/ConfirmModal/Toast - Hardcoded secrets in any generated template -- always reference env vars - Raw timestamps in maintenance history -- use relative time formatting - Delete/trigger without confirmation -- "Run Now" button requires confirmation
ui_ux_standards.required_components: - Toast notification after manual maintenance trigger (success: "Maintenance started", error: "Failed to start") - Loading spinner on "Run Now" button during API call - Skeleton loader for maintenance history table while loading - EmptyState for maintenance tab when no runs exist ("No maintenance runs yet") - ConfirmModal before manual maintenance trigger
ui_ux_standards.feedback_protocol: - Trigger maintenance: confirm modal -> loading state -> toast + refresh history - Settings save: loading button -> toast ("Settings saved") + close modal - Report load: skeleton -> rendered report or error state with retry

coding_standards.architecture: - Follow existing AutoForge patterns: new routers in server/routers/, new services in server/services/, new components in ui/src/components/ - Python: SQLAlchemy models in api/database.py, FastAPI routers with Pydantic request/response models - TypeScript: interfaces in ui/src/lib/types.ts, API functions in ui/src/lib/api.ts, TanStack Query hooks in ui/src/hooks/ - All new Python code must pass ruff check and mypy - All new TypeScript code must pass npm run lint and npm run build
coding_standards.error_handling: - Maintenance trigger endpoint returns 404 if project not found, 409 if maintenance already running - Auto-update agent failures logged to MaintenanceRun.error_message and surfaced in UI - Graceful degradation: if gh CLI unavailable, skip PR/issue creation and note in report - Scheduler errors logged but do not crash the server

key_interactions.trigger_maintenance_flow: 1. User navigates to project's Maintenance tab 2. User clicks "Run Now" button 3. ConfirmModal appears asking "Start maintenance run for {project}?" 4. User confirms, button shows loading spinner 5. POST /trigger API spawns auto-update agent subprocess 6. Toast shows "Maintenance started for {project}" 7. History table auto-refreshes via TanStack Query invalidation 8. When run completes, new row appears in history with status badge
key_interactions.configure_devops_flow: 1. User opens Settings modal (comma key or gear icon) 2. User scrolls to DevOps section 3. User selects deployment target from dropdown 4. User checks/unchecks monitoring features 5. User selects update strategy (conservative/aggressive) 6. User picks maintenance frequency (weekly/biweekly/monthly) 7. User clicks Save, settings persisted via PUT /api/settings 8. Toast confirms "Settings saved"
key_interactions.post_build_agent_flow: 1. All project features reach PASSING status 2. Orchestrator detects build completion via _check_post_build_ready() 3. CI/CD agent spawns, reads project, generates pipeline files 4. Monitoring agent spawns in parallel, modifies existing files to add observability 5. Both agents complete as single-turn subprocesses 6. Agent status updates sent via WebSocket to UI 7. Project view shows post-build completion status
key_interactions.view_maintenance_report_flow: 1. User views maintenance history in Maintenance tab 2. User clicks expand arrow on a history row 3. GET /report/{run_id} fetches the markdown report 4. Report renders inline with formatted tables for dependencies, security audit, and test results 5. If PR was created, clickable link opens GitHub PR in new tab 6. If issue was created on failure, clickable link opens GitHub issue

success_criteria.functionality: - All three agent types (cicd, monitoring, auto-update) can be launched via CLI and via the UI agent start endpoint - CI/CD agent generates complete GitHub Actions workflows, Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, .env.example, and Makefile for a target project - Monitoring agent correctly modifies existing project files to add Sentry, health endpoints, and structured logging - Auto-update agent performs the full audit-update-verify-report-commit/rollback workflow - Maintenance history persists across server restarts in SQLite - Maintenance schedules fire at the correct intervals via the scheduler service - Post-build agents automatically spawn when all features pass in parallel orchestrator mode
success_criteria.user_experience: - Maintenance tab provides clear visibility into maintenance run history and status - Settings modal DevOps section allows configuring all three agents without touching config files - Manual maintenance trigger provides immediate feedback with toast notification - Maintenance reports render cleanly with formatted tables and clickable PR/issue links - Empty states guide users to configure maintenance when no runs exist
success_criteria.technical_quality: - All Python code passes ruff check . and mypy - All TypeScript code passes npm run lint and npm run build in ui/ - No console errors in the React UI - Database migrations are backward-compatible (new columns have defaults, new table is additive) - Post-build agents do not interfere with coding agents or with each other - Auto-update agent never force-pushes, never merges its own PRs, and always rolls back cleanly on failure
